attrs.why: Refines the frontier 'white dot syndrome' (node-5, belief 0.8) into its most specific leading subtype. MEWDS is the commonest white dot syndrome and matches the entire evidence set: young myopic woman with acute unilateral vision loss/metamorphopsia (node-1), posterior-pole yellow-white spots (node-4), quiet anterior chamber and vitreous (node-3), SD-OCT focal ellipsoid zone elevation with hyper-reflective material (node-8), intact RPE/Bruch's membrane and no CNV (node-9), and no CNV on OCTA (node-11). Confidence held at 0.7 pending FAF/FA/ICGA/ERG confirmation.

Subtype refinement of 'white dot syndrome' (node-5) that presents with acute visual loss and outer retinal/ellipsoid-zone disruption, so the SD-OCT EZ findings (node-8) permit it. However, AZOOR typically lacks the transient posterior-pole yellow-white spots seen here (node-4) and is less typical for this young myopic profile; FAF/ERG would be needed to separate it from MEWDS.

A further white-dot-syndrome subcategory plausible in young myopic women, refining node-5. It is weakened by the absence of choroidal neovascularization on SD-OCT/OCTA (nodes 9, 11), the lack of vitreous inflammation (node-3), and the absence of hemorrhage on fundoscopy (node-4), all of which argue against the typical MFC/PIC picture.
